subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: If a sealed container of gas is heated, the pressure increases because the particles:
options: Move faster and hit the walls more often and harder
Become heavier
Stick together
Move closer together
questions.explain: Heating gives the particles more kinetic energy, so they collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force.

questions.q: When light passes from glass into air (along a line not on the normal), it bends:
options: Away from the normal because it speeds up
Back the way it came
It does not bend at all
Towards the normal because it slows down
questions.explain: Light speeds up when it enters a less dense medium (glass to air), so it refracts away from the normal.

questions.q: Which of these quantities is a scalar?
options: Displacement
Force
Acceleration
Distance
questions.explain: A scalar has magnitude only. Distance is a scalar; force, displacement and acceleration all have direction, so they are vectors. (Distance vs displacement is a common trap.)

questions.q: On a free-body diagram of a book resting on a table, which two forces are shown acting on the book?
options: Two equal friction forces
Only the weight
Weight upward and friction downward
Weight downward and the normal contact (reaction) force upward
questions.explain: The book's weight acts downward and the table pushes up with an equal normal contact (reaction) force. As they balance, the resultant force is zero and the book stays still.

questions.q: When ice melts to form water, what happens to the total mass?
options: It stays the same
It increases
It becomes zero
It decreases
questions.explain: Melting is a physical change: no particles are created or destroyed, so mass is conserved. The water has the same mass as the ice it came from.

questions.q: As light passes from air into a glass block along a path at an angle to the normal, it bends:
options: Toward the normal because it slows down
Straight back the way it came
It does not bend at all
Away from the normal because it speeds up
questions.explain: Glass is more optically dense than air, so light slows down on entering. This makes the ray bend toward the normal. Going the other way (glass to air) it speeds up and bends away from the normal.

questions.q: What is the difference between elastic and inelastic deformation?
options: Elastic deformation returns to the original shape when the force is removed; inelastic does not
They are the same thing
Elastic deformation is permanent; inelastic returns to shape
Inelastic only happens to metals
questions.explain: In elastic deformation the object returns to its original shape once the force is removed. In inelastic (plastic) deformation it does not fully return — it is permanently changed.

questions.q: What causes the pressure of a gas on the walls of its container?
options: The particles sticking to the walls
The weight of the gas particles resting on the walls
Gas particles colliding with the walls and exerting a force
The walls attracting the particles
questions.explain: Gas pressure is caused by particles colliding with the container walls; each collision exerts a tiny force, and the total over the wall area gives the pressure.

questions.q: In the required practical, how can you measure the speed of waves in a ripple tank?
options: Measure the amplitude and double it
Time how long the tank takes to fill
Measure only the depth of water
Measure the frequency and wavelength, then use v = fλ
questions.explain: You find the frequency (e.g. from the wave generator or by counting waves per second) and the wavelength (e.g. from a stroboscope or by measuring several waves), then calculate v = fλ.

questions.q: Specific latent heat is the energy needed to:
options: Melt only metals
Increase the pressure of a gas
Raise the temperature of a substance
Change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature
questions.explain: Specific latent heat is the energy needed to change the state of 1 kg of a substance at constant temperature.

questions.q: An object floats on water. How does the upthrust compare with the object's weight?
options: Upthrust is greater than the weight
Upthrust is less than the weight
Upthrust is zero
Upthrust equals the weight
questions.explain: A floating object is in equilibrium, so the upthrust (upward) exactly balances the weight (downward). If upthrust were less, it would sink; if more, it would rise.

questions.q: Compared with the same substance as a solid, the particles in a gas have:
options: Less energy and are closer together
The same energy but a fixed shape
No energy at all
More energy and are much further apart
questions.explain: Gas particles have more kinetic energy and are far apart, moving quickly in random directions.

questions.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass changes with location; weight does not
Weight is measured in kilograms; mass in newtons
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on it (N)
They are the same thing measured in different units
questions.explain: Mass is the quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms, and is the same everywhere. Weight is the gravitational force on that mass, measured in newtons, and depends on the gravitational field strength.

questions.q: Which quantity is measured in a derived unit rather than an SI base unit?
options: Time, in seconds
Length, in metres
Mass, in kilograms
Speed, in metres per second
questions.explain: A derived unit is built from base units. Speed (m/s) is metres divided by seconds, so it is derived. The second, metre and kilogram are SI base units.

questions.q: Which statement about the particle model is correct?
options: Particles in a solid are far apart
Particles in a liquid are arranged in a fixed regular pattern
Particles in a liquid can move past one another but stay close together
Particles in a gas vibrate about fixed positions
questions.explain: In a liquid the particles are close together but free to move and flow past each other.

questions.q: How do all electromagnetic waves travel through a vacuum?
options: Only visible light can travel through a vacuum
All at the same speed (the speed of light)
At different speeds depending on frequency
They cannot travel through a vacuum
questions.explain: All EM waves are transverse and travel at the same speed (about 3 × 10⁸ m/s) through a vacuum. They differ in frequency and wavelength, not speed in a vacuum.

questions.q: A solid object floats on water. What can you conclude about its density?
options: It is greater than the density of water
It has no density because it floats
It is less than the density of water
It is equal to the density of water
questions.explain: An object floats when its mean density is less than that of the fluid (water, 1000 kg/m³); denser objects sink.

questions.q: In what direction do magnetic field lines around a bar magnet point?
options: From south pole to north pole outside the magnet
Always towards the nearest pole
In random directions
From north pole to south pole outside the magnet
questions.explain: By convention, magnetic field lines travel from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. The direction is the direction of the force on a north pole.

questions.q: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as you go higher up a mountain?
options: The air becomes a liquid
Gravity disappears at altitude
The air gets colder
There is less air (a shorter column of air) above you pressing down
questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air above. Higher up, there is less air above you and it is less dense, so the pressure is lower.

questions.q: How are the particles arranged in a solid?
options: Far apart and moving randomly
Close together but able to flow past each other
Spread out evenly with large gaps
Close together in a regular fixed pattern
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are packed closely in a regular arrangement and only vibrate about fixed positions.

questions.q: Heating a substance without changing its state increases its internal energy by:
options: Increasing the kinetic energy of its particles
Removing particles
Changing the chemical formula
Reducing the speed of the particles
questions.explain: Heating increases the kinetic energy of the particles, raising the temperature and internal energy.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph for a spring obeying Hooke's law, the line is:
options: A curve that flattens off
A horizontal line
A curve that gets steeper
A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: While a spring obeys Hooke's law, force is directly proportional to extension, so the force–extension graph is a straight line through the origin. The gradient equals the spring constant k.
